name: Russia
genZNote: Spans 11 time zones and two continents at once — Russia's map alone is basically a geography exam question.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The world's largest country by area, spanning Eastern Europe and Northern Asia across 11 time zones.
The Ural Mountains are traditionally considered the geographic boundary between European and Asian Russia.
Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is the world's deepest freshwater lake and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Capital: Moscow; second city: St. Petersburg.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Russian is the official language; the country is ethnically diverse, with over 190 recognised ethnic groups.
A major contributor to world literature (Tolstoy, Dostoevsky), classical music (Tchaikovsky), and ballet.
The Moscow Kremlin and Red Square are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal semi-presidential republic; the President is head of state, the Prime Minister heads the government.
Bicameral Federal Assembly: State Duma (lower house) and Federation Council (upper house).
Formed as the Russian Federation following the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A pioneering space power — launched Sputnik 1 (1957, first artificial satellite) and sent Yuri Gagarin (1961, first human in space) via the Soviet-era space programme.
Roscosmos, its space agency, remains a key partner in the International Space Station programme.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A permanent member of the UN Security Council; member of BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).
One of the world's largest producers and exporters of oil and natural gas.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Russia describe their ties as a 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership', with roots going back to the Soviet era.
Long-standing defence cooperation, including major defence equipment supply and joint development programmes (e.g. the BrahMos missile, jointly developed with India).
Energy trade (notably crude oil) has grown significantly as part of the bilateral economic relationship.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Heavily reliant on natural resource exports — oil, natural gas, and minerals form the backbone of its export economy.
A major global arms exporter, alongside the US, France, and China.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the world's largest country by area, spanning 11 time zones across Europe and Asia.
Pioneering achievements in space exploration (Sputnik, Gagarin) and a long-standing strategic partnership with India.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Russian Ruble (RUB).
The world's largest country by land area, spanning eleven time zones, with an economy heavily reliant on oil, natural gas, and mineral exports.
A major global supplier of energy resources, notably natural gas to European markets.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to Siberia's vast taiga, the world's largest forest biome.
Lake Baikal is the world's deepest and oldest freshwater lake, holding roughly a fifth of the planet's unfrozen fresh water.
Significant Arctic territory and permafrost regions are highly sensitive to climate change.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Traces statehood to Kievan Rus' and the later Tsardom and Empire of Russia.
The 1917 Revolution ended tsarist rule and led to the founding of the Soviet Union.
The USSR dissolved in 1991, giving rise to the Russian Federation and several other independent states.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1917 Revolution ended monarchy and established Soviet rule.
1991 dissolution of the USSR created the modern Russian Federation.
The 1993 Constitution established a semi-presidential system of government.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Roscosmos is one of the pioneering space agencies — launched Sputnik in 1957, the first artificial satellite, and sent Yuri Gagarin as the first human in space in 1961.
Continues to operate crewed missions to the International Space Station via Soyuz spacecraft.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Strong tradition in classical ballet, centred on the Bolshoi Theatre, and classical literature including Tolstoy and Dostoevsky.
Hosted the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics and the 2018 FIFA World Cup.
Chess has deep cultural roots and a long history of world-champion players.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: A permanent member of the UN Security Council.
Member of BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO); suspended from the G8 (now G7) in 2014.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Russia is the world's largest country by area, a federal semi-presidential republic spanning Europe and Asia, and a long-standing strategic partner of India.
keyFacts: World's largest country by area, spanning 11 time zones.
Permanent UN Security Council member; formed in 1991 after the Soviet Union's dissolution.
India-Russia ties: 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'.
commonConfusion: The Soviet Union dissolved in 1991 — Russia (the Russian Federation) is its main successor state, not identical to it.

highYieldFacts: Russia is a permanent UN Security Council member and spans 11 time zones — the largest country by area on Earth.
BrahMos is a jointly developed India-Russia missile system, a frequently tested India-Russia defence-cooperation fact.
commonTraps: Treating 'Soviet Union' and 'Russia' as fully interchangeable — Russia is the largest successor state after the USSR's 1991 dissolution, not the same entity.
mustRemember: Russia: permanent UNSC member, world's largest country by area, 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership' with India.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Russia Relations
